record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can formal theory for knowledge-base exchange, including universal solutions, universal UCQ-solutions, and UCQ-representations for DL-LiteR knowledge bases, guide knowledge-base mapping generation tools that consider target constraints, and can that theory be used to create tools whose generated mappings have specified formal properties?

evidence.quote: An important research question is how to use this formal work to guide KMGTs and if we can use the theory to create tools that produce mappings with certain formal properties.

artifact.category_tag: Knowledge base exchange in description logics
artifact.status_search_result: The theoretical foundations for knowledge-base exchange in DL-Lite_R (universal solutions, universal UCQ-solutions, UCQ-representations, with associated complexity results) are well developed, notably by Arenas, Botoeva, Calvanese, Ryzhikov and Sherkhonov. However, the question of leveraging this theory to drive practical knowledge-base mapping generation tools whose outputs come with these certified formal properties is posed as a direction for future research and has no published constructive algorithm or completeness theorem connecting KMGTs to (a)–(c). The status therefore appears open.

status_evidence.title: Exchanging OWL 2 QL Knowledge Bases
status_evidence.snippet: Defines and analyzes universal solutions, universal UCQ-solutions, and UCQ-representations for DL-Lite_R knowledge bases, with complexity results, but does not address mapping-generation tools.
status_evidence.claim: The underlying formal theory exists but does not address constructive mapping-generation tools.

status_evidence.title: Knowledge base exchange: The case of OWL 2 QL
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the existence and computation of universal solutions and UCQ-representations for OWL 2 QL / DL-Lite_R knowledge bases.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the theoretical machinery referenced in the problem, leaving the tool-building question open.
